meta.description: Simple starting points for common needs young adults may have.

pathways.title: I need a safe place tonight
pathways.summary: Start with the local program that helps people who do not have a safe place to stay. If you cannot reach it or it does not fit, try the statewide help line next.
documents: Photo ID, if you have one
Where you are now and a safe phone number
Any eviction, move-out or program-exit notice
Names and ages of anyone who needs to stay with you
successCriteria: You talk with someone about what is happening
You know who to contact, where to go or when to follow up
You know whether the program can help
You have another option when no bed or housing is open
pathways.limit: Shelter beds and emergency housing may not be open. Talking with a program does not promise a place to stay. Call 911 if you are in immediate danger.

pathways.title: I may lose my housing soon
pathways.summary: Contact a housing-help program before your deadline. Gather any papers that show when you have to leave, and keep following up until you know whether the program can help.
documents: Your lease or written housing agreement
Any eviction, move-out or program-exit notice
Photo ID, if you have one
Information about your income, benefits and household
The date you may have to leave
successCriteria: You know what papers are needed and how to apply
You have a date to follow up
You have another option if money or openings are unavailable
pathways.limit: Many housing programs cannot help right away. They may require a written notice, proof that you live in the county or other specific information. Do not assume an application is approved until the program tells you.

pathways.title: I need help with more than one thing
pathways.summary: Start with a program that can help you sort out what is most urgent, find the right programs and make a simple plan instead of calling a long list on your own.
documents: A short list of your two or three most urgent needs
Photo ID and proof of address, if you have them
Information about your income and benefits
Any applications or letters you have already received
The deadline for each urgent need
successCriteria: You choose the most urgent need first
You know which program or action goes with each need
You know what could slow down an application and what papers you need
You set a date to follow up on anything still unresolved
pathways.limit: A program can help you make a plan, but it cannot create openings that do not exist. When a program is full, ask when to check again and what else you can try.
